Cane Brothers #1

Dragoste la prima avere

Meghan Quinn, Maria Adam (translator)

4.00
292,557 ratings25,009 reviews
Rate this book
Un roman de dragoste cu accente comice despre un miliardar disperat care își caută logodnică și, totodată, o abordare modernă, incredibil de inteligentă și amuzantă a poveștii din Pretty Woman, care te va face să dai pagină după pagină!

„Cum v-ați întâlnit?” Întrebarea de bază de care are parte orice cuplu. Iar răspunsul este de obicei o poveste siropoasă despre cum ați ajuns voi doi în cătarea arcului lui Cupidon.

Întâlnirea mea romantică (mă rog, nu chiar așa de romantică) este puțin diferită. Mă plimbam printr-un cartier exclusivist din Beverly Hills în căutarea cuiva care să mă ia de nevastă, nu de alta, dar ca s-o fac geloasă pe dușmanca mea, care tocmai mă concediase. El a apărut de după colț, un căpcăun superb care bălmăjea ceva despre o afacere pe care nu reușea să o încheie, așa că era disperat să găsească o soluție.

Și atunci am dat nas în nas. Nicio scânteie. Niciun indiciu că între noi ar putea înflori iubirea.

Următorul lucru pe care mi-l aduc aminte e că mă îndopam cu cartofi prăjiți și guacamole, ascultându-l pe bărbatul acesta superb povestindu-mi despre problemele lui, care într-un final l-au determinat să îmi ceară ajutorul. Mai exact, m-a rugat să joc pentru el rolul lui Vivian Ward, știi tu, personajul din Pretty Woman, minus partea flușturatică.

Adică să locuim împreună într-o vilă, să ieșim la întâlniri romantice duble și să ne prefacem că suntem nu numai îndrăgostiți până peste cap unul de celălalt, ci și logodiți. Îți imaginezi? Nebunia supremă!

Dar oamenii fac lucruri nebunești atunci când sunt disperați, iar eu chiar eram pe culmile disperării. În concluzie, am fost de acord.

Singura mea greșeală? Singura mea mare… URIAȘĂ… greșeală? M-am îndrăgostit de extraordinarul domn Huxley Cane!

When I was in high school I occasionally read books but was consumed by other teenage things so I didn't take the time to appreciate a good book on a cloudy day, wrapped up in a blanket on the couch. It wasn't until I received a Kindle for Christmas one year that my world completely flipped upside down. When looking for books I came across the Contemporary Romance genre and was sold and I haven't turned back since.

You can either find my head buried in my Kindle, listening to inspiring heart ripping music or typing away on the computer twisting and turning the lives of my characters while driving my readers crazy with anticipation.

​I currently reside in beautiful Colorado Springs where the sun is always shining and there is a trail waiting to be hiked on every corner. I share a lovely and warm home with the love of my life and my five, four-legged children.

This started our very well. I was hooked because I really wanted to read this trope and enjoy some light angst and funny bits.

BUT

It started to drag and then it just kept on dragging. (Apart from some funny scenes here and there the plot just wasn’t very interesting past the 20/30% mark)
The heroine was not likeable past the beginning of the book. She was inexplicably mean and childish in her behaviour towards the hero. While I’m not gonna say that he was some great paragon of virtue - he was just a normal guy who made a deal and paid out huge amounts of money for what was simply a few hours of her pretending to “love” him in front of someone else.

She was absolutely broke and basically homeless and not only he paid off her student debt, but he bought her clothes and shoes and jewellery that she wouldn’t have afforded in 10 years if she saved up every pay check. He also let her live with him and provided all meals for her. And on top of all that - he helped her sister’s (and her) new startup business flourish. And what did she do? Constantly insulted him and trying to back out of the deal because he was cold towards her. Excuse me? He was not mean, or insulting, or bad tempered or anything that would make him the bad guy. He just had a distant disposition towards her and that offended her broke-ass sensibilities. Bitch please?!

Her sister calls her out, and what does she do.. gets to thinking for a bit and I thought she was gonna realise her immature attitude but no .. eventually she still had to be right.

And her whole drama about how her friend betrayed her? No. She’s got no sympathy from me. She knew the woman for more than 10 years. She was not a victim - she willingly wanted to profit from her friendship with that woman even if she treated her bad and the odds were 50/50 that she was gonna get screwed.

The hero was just a normal, nice guy underneath his extreme drive and ambition in the business world.

think of a bowl of m&m’s or snickers, but make it a book 😋

i don’t remember when was the last time i laughed out loud to a rom-com, which makes me so happy that this book made me laugh numerous times because divine rivals was side-eyeing me in my mind. however the banter was incredibly funny that it got me out of the hangover; but the reason i enjoyed the book this much was the star of this book, lottie.

“You’re so narcissistic.”
“Confident,” he replies.
“A cockhole.”
His brows raise. “What the hell is a cockhole?”
“Cocky asshole. Therefore, you’re a cockhole.”

so, if you are looking for a book that is easy to read with light writing and many funny scenes, this is exactly what you should pick up. it’s entertaining, fast paced and incredibly cute.

basically the plot is lottie, fmc, got fired from her job due to her toxic friend, who is her boss, and she started to search for a rich husband in a rich neighborhood to pay her school debt. in the mean time, huxley, mmc, lied about that he is engaged and his fiancee is pregnant to one his biggest clients in order to create a friendly connection between them. while lottie was searching for a husband, they bump into each other and decide that they should make a fake marriage deal.

i know it sounds so unrealistic and ridiculous, but if you read the book with no expectations of it being a huge masterpiece, you will enjoy every second of it, because both lottie and hux was incredibly entertaining characters.

“When I said hard, I meant something like “Who would you die on a sword for? Team Jacob or Team Edward?” Side note . . . glitter dick, all day, every day.”

lottie: funniest protagonist i have ever read. the second i read that she imagined that the imperial march was playing in hux's head because he looked so emotionless, i knew i was going to love her. aside for her funny personality, she was confident, realistic, honest and strong, which are all the traits i adore in a person. she was mature enough to admit that her fear of conflict made her pursue her friendship with angela; she was aware that she was a toxic friend, but her actions didn’t make lottie to question her capabilities, instead she was always conscious of how much of a strong and skilled woman she is. also she was so straightforward, she didn’t hesitate to question hux’s actions and she has always been honest about her feelings.

”Need a place to stay? I have a seven-bedroom home. Need a date for your reunion? I’m your man. Need me to make a phone call to this ex-boss of yours, let her know she made a huge mistake by letting you go? I’m there for you. Want a job? I can find you one.”

huxley: another mmc whose love language is acts of service… i am sold. in the first chapter he didn’t let his assistant go get him lunch because he was well capable of doing that and he loves to walk made me smiling in the first place, but when he lied about his fiancee was pregnant, he instantly felt disgust towards himself because he thought about all the women who tries to get pregnant but just can’t.. it was such a thoughtful mindset, i loved him in that second. relating to a male character is not something i experience a lot but the duality he went through, wanting to be the best but getting anxious when he gets compliments was something that i can feel so deeply. even though he was scared to open himself to lottie, he was never disrespectful or close to communication, he always stated that he wants lottie to tell him when she feels uncomfortable and made sure she is comfortable around him.

what i mean by acts of service was; him giving lottie his best car so she can travel between the houses of her family easily, sending the pictures of jeff’s (lottie’s step father) garden to garden committee so they can win the best garden prize, sending flowers to lottie’s mom to congratulate her, arranging his whole work schedule so kelsey (lottie’s sister) can present her business to him.. he cares about lottie, and lottie cares about those people, so he made his business to keep them all happy. he also sent meals and desserts for the families of the workers who has been wounded in one of his buildings; he is incredibly kind and thoughtful. he even remembered that one of lottie's wishes was to lay in rain, so the second it rained he took her to roof and laid down in rain with her. he even took her to her favorite artist’s concert, how can you not love him when all he does is showing he cares about her?

”What on Earth is this?”
“An engagement ring.” he says casually.
“Uh, this isn’t engagement ring, this is an ice rink for a family of five.”

the banter. it was so realistic, funny and smart that, it become my favorite thing about the book. i don’t want to give too much spoilers so i will keep it simple but the double dates they went with dave and ellie.. the pregnancy classes.. i can’t even count the times i giggled and kicked my feet.

the last thing i adored was sibling relationships. both lottie’s and huxley’s relationship with their siblings were presented so well; their need for each other, endless love, their communication, always backing each other up and trying to make others happy was such a cute detail in this book.

“She’s not what I was expecting. But she’s everything I fucking want.”

replace ‘she’ with 'this book', and this is what i think about a not so meet cute. i would definitely recommend this if you feel like you are getting into a slump, or just want to laugh your ass off without expecting too much 💗

oct 18: okayy this book saved me from a major slump so even though it wasn’t a masterpiece, i want to write a good review for it heheh 🤭 so rtc!

oct 14: me desperately searching for a good read after divine rivals.. pls universe, let me enjoy this 😭

So many situations were so over the top and the story just dragged on. As a contemporary romance, it needs to be faster paced if it's going to be 400 pages long. Even when they actually get together, I was bored. And then the third act break up included one of my least favorite tropes and I was just not having it. There was a conversation at the end the kind of made the over-the-top scenes make sense to me, but it still didn't make them enjoyable. I'm not sure Meghan Quinn is more me and it's going to be awhile before I pick up one of her rom coms.

Disclaimer: I usually don't hate heroines, it's too much of a strong feeling for me to experience towards a written character, but this time i wanted to slap the heroine, Lottie, across the face. Repeatedly. With a shovel. 👁️👄👁️

So the plot: Lottie, a 28year old down on her luck, gets fired by her "friend", needs to move out from her parents ASAP, has only 3 grand in her bank account and 30K of student loans. Living in LA, this is not enough to cover rent, so she gets drunk with her sister and has the "marvelous" idea to go to the rich neighborhood and find a rich husband to solve all of her problems. In an old, ratty T-Shirt with holes in it 👉👈🥹 First day is a bust, so instead of actually sending out a couple of résumés to potential bosses (did I mention she has a degree in business?🤡🤡🤡🫣), she decides to go AGAIN in search of a rich husband. Enter the hero, Huxley, a 35year old billionaire 🤣 who needed to close a 10 mil deal SOOOO BADLY that he lied to a potential partner about having a pregnant fiancee from Georgia. Huxley is terrified his deal will fall through plus bis reputation will be ruined, so instead of coming clean or telling one of his NUMEROUS ASSISTANTS (that a true billionaire will 100% have) to contact some acting agency (it's LA, come on!) and hire an actress to play the fiancée, he goes on a walk to "clear his head" 🕵️🤨 He then meets Lottie on the street, where she rambles about needing a rich husband, so he jumps on the opportunity and everything starts from there.

Now, this is one of those books, where in order to make it funny, the author made it OTT unbelievable. Plus, the hero, a supposed billionaire, has the personality of a dead fish and nothing unique about his thought process, way of thinking or acting, his business plan to make him a billionaire. It was so farfetched, so it felt completely unnecessary. The author should've made him at least a millionaire, so that his attempt to close a 10 mil deal would seam somewhat more logical. All in all, Huxley was not a bad hero, but he was also not good: bland, unmemorable, mediocre. I didn't like his hot and cold game he played around the middle of the book, and the reasoning behind it was weak.

But the real assholette of this book was the heroine. I barely finished the book, that's how infuriating she was to me! 🤬🤬🤬🤬 It wasn't even the situation she found herself in and the way she tried to resolve it (although combating homelessness and unemployment with just taking a stroll in a rich neighborhood is up there), but her reaction towards everything around her and her victim mentality.

- the hero was basically a stranger to her, who payed off 30K of her student loans, bought her an expensive designer wardrobe, gave her a roof over her head (a stylish McMansion), and even fed her gourmet meals on the daily. All she had to do on exchange, was to play his pregnant fiancee a couple of times and "suffer" through uncomfortable outings with the pregnant chick. Lottie CONSTANTLY complained about how the hero was CoLd towards her (while they were still strangers with a shared goal), so she irritated him to no end, tried to be funny, which resulted in her looking like a fool all of the time.

-Lottie and Huxely signed a contract with ALL of the terms, explanations and rules regarding their "partnership". You'd think that a person with a BUSINESS DEGREE would read the damn thing, but our hilariously dumb heroine thought it unnecessary. And didn't actually mean anything 😭😭😭 #helphowisshesodumb

- Lottie's sister, Kelsey, gave her a job, even though she couldn't afford to do it. They got a meeting with a potential client (Huxely's BILLION dollar firm), the sister is rushing there to get on time, to which Lottie says "Don't worry, we still have 2 minutes, just RELAAAX" 😫 the sister explains the significance of this meeting and asks Lottie to take it seriously. Minutes later, Lottie makes a complete fool of herself, embarrasses herself, her sister, sits on Huxely's lap and tries to kiss him, while looking scared and confused. Overall Opinion: This had some fun moments! It was a pretty light drama, funny, and sexy read. I just didn’t like the h. I also thought that the H had to grovel way too much for his wrongdoing — which is a change! It might be that I liked the H at that point and didn’t like the h, but it just didn’t work for me. Overall, as long as you go in just expecting some laughs and low drama sexiness…this should work for you.

Brief Summary of the Storyline: This is Lottie and Huxley’s story. Huxley has unintentionally lied to a potential client that he has a pregnant fiancé, so when he literally bumps into a down-on-her-luck and ranting about finding a rich husband Lottie, he knows that she is the answer to save his and his brothers’ company from potential reputation ruin. Lottie just got fired by her on-again-off-again best “friend” and is also desperately needing to move out of her mother’s house, so when Huxley propositions her she accepts the pretty woman style (without the nookie) deal. There are some laugh out loud moments, some hot sexy times, and some big secrets revealed…and they get a HFN ending.

Point Of View (POV): This alternated between Lottie and Huxley’s POV.

Overall Pace of Story: Good. I never skimmed and I thought it flowed well.

Instalove: No, they take a while to develop stronger feelings

H (Hero) rating: 3.5 stars. Huxley. I mostly liked him. I appreciated his grovel, but his hot and cold at the beginning got a little old.

h (heroine) rating: 2.5 stars. Lottie. I really struggled with her. I felt like she was too self-centered a lot of the time.

Sadness level: Low, no tissues needed

Push/Pull: Yes

Heat level: Hot. They have some hot tension, chemistry, and scenes -- but not so much it takes away from the story.

Descriptive sex: Yes

OW (Other Woman)/OM (Other Man) drama: No

Sex scene with OW or OM: No

Cheating: No

Separation: Yes

Possible Triggers: Not really

Closure: This ends in a good place but with what I would call a HFN ending

Safety: This one should be Safe for most safety gang readers

Kelsey: Oh my God . . . you’re going to be murdered.
Lottie: No way. The dude is meeting me at Chipotle. He’s not going to murder me at a place where you have to pay extra for guac.


Lottie (26) gets fired by one of her supposedly close friends, Angela, and is escorted out of the building as soon as she is. She goes home to her mom’s house, who is expecting her to get a promotion the following week so she can finally get her own place (because her mom and younger boyfriend like walking around she house… naked 😅😂). She’s afraid to tell her what happened, because her family has constantly told her not to trust Angela. She pretends to go to work but really goes to her sister’s to make a plan. One of her plans is to meet a rich hubby, Pretty Woman style, and hopefully get all her prayers answered. Well, she does…

Huxley (35) is trying to sign a deal, a very profitable one, and he makes the mistake of lying by saying that he has a fiancé that’s also pregnant, just like the investor he’s trying to get to sign the deal (he has a pregnant fiancé). Now he’s on a time crunch to find a fake fiancé that’s pregnant. Lo and behold, Lottie smacks into his life- and she agrees to sign a contract as long as she gets something out of the deal as well (she’s poor and needs her student loans paid off plus an action plan for the business she’s starting with her sister). ”I’m also going to need your ring size. My fiancée will be properly adorned with a ring.”

“Because,” she says with a smile, “I need to know if I have to act like a happy fiancée, or a truly satisfied fiancée.”

╰┈➤ 💌 : a not so meet cute ★★☆☆☆ ⋆˙⟡

☆ ── ꒰ 📖 “sometimes the cutest meet cutes are the ones that make you question everything” ꒱ ❞ ‧₊˚

𖥻 my thoughts 🎀 ₊˚⊹ ᰔ

i went into this with SUCH high hopes because fake dating + romcom vibes + pretty woman inspired?? yeah i was READY 😭💌. pretty woman is literally one of my favourite movies, so when i saw this was inspired by it, i thought i was going to absolutely love it. especially because i was already in a little book slump and i wanted something light, funny, and easy to enjoy 🫶🏼✨

and honestly… the beginning had me!! i was actually hooked 🤭. the random meet cute, the fake relationship deal, the whole “we need to pretend to be together” situation was so fun and had so much potential 💍. i really thought i found the perfect fluffy romance to get me out of my slump.

BUT… then it started dragging. and dragging. and dragging 😭📖. after around the 20–30% mark, i just felt myself losing interest. apart from a few funny scenes here and there, the plot just wasn’t keeping me entertained anymore 🫠. for a contemporary romance that is almost 400 pages, i needed it to move faster because at some point i was just waiting for something to happen.

my biggest issue was honestly the characters 😓. i really struggled with lottie because at first i liked her, but then she became so mean and childish towards huxley for reasons that didn’t fully make sense to me. like i understand wanting emotional connection and wanting someone to be warm towards you, but the constant insults and pushing him away started feeling exhausting 😭. it felt less like playful banter and more like they were just hurting each other.

and huxley… i had mixed feelings 🫣. i don’t think he was this horrible villain that the book tried to make him seem sometimes. yes, he was cold and very business-focused, but he literally helped her so much?? like paying off her student debt, buying her things, letting her stay with him, helping her family and her business… and then they would have these huge arguments where i was just sitting there like ??? 😭

the whole dynamic between them just gave me the biggest ick sometimes 🫠. there was so much “you hurt me” and then two seconds later “i’m yours” energy and i was like girl PLEASE pick a side 😭💀. the emotional whiplash was insane.

also… the amount of sexual comments about lottie’s body really did not work for me 😭. i know it’s romance and attraction is obviously part of it, but sometimes it felt like that was the main way huxley viewed her and it made some moments uncomfortable instead of romantic.

𖥻 characters 💐 ౨ৎ˚₊‧ִֶ

⋆˙⟡ lottie 🩷

lottie started off really cute and fun, and i genuinely wanted to love her 🥹. i liked her confidence and her personality in the beginning, but as the story continued i found myself getting more frustrated with her choices. she was supposed to be this fun, outspoken, spunky heroine, but sometimes it crossed into being unnecessarily mean 😓. i wanted to understand her more, but a lot of her actions just didn’t land for me.

⋆˙⟡ huxley 🖤

huxley was… complicated 🫠. i understood the appeal people saw in him because he had that intense, successful, protective vibe, but some moments really didn’t work for me. the whole “i own you” energy and the demanding behaviour felt strange, especially because this was marketed as a rom-com 😭.

there were sweet moments though, like when he genuinely cared about her and helped her. i just wish the book balanced his softer side with the intense side better.

⋆˙⟡ lottie + huxley 💌

i really wanted to root for them 😭💍. the fake dating trope is literally one of my favourites, but their relationship just didn’t feel healthy or developed enough for me. there was attraction, yes, but i didn’t feel the emotional connection building.

the third act especially… no 😭. the conflict felt messy, and the resolution with the engagement after only FIVE WEEKS??? girl what 😭💀. i needed more growth, more understanding, more actual getting to know each other.

₊⁺ 𖥻 overall 🧺 ⋆.˚୨ৎ

i’m honestly so sad this one didn’t work for me because the beginning had SO much potential 🥲💌. the premise was cute, the idea was fun, and there were moments that genuinely made me laugh, but the pacing, the romance, and some of the character choices just gave me the biggest ick.

i really wanted to understand the hype because everyone seems to love this one, but unfortunately it just wasn’t for me 😭📚. maybe this author’s writing style isn’t my vibe, but i’m glad i tried it.

⋆.˚ ★— started: 23rd June
finished: DNF 💔

December 6, 2021
⭐️ one star -

Ok, I hated this book. Truly. It pains me to say this because I generally do enjoy Meghan Quinn’s NA genre stories, but her last few adult romances have been horrible. I thought I’d give her another chance with this one as the story seemed interesting - meet cute with a billionaire and a 28 yo fmc? Sounded great, especially since I prefer stories with adults vs the na genre romances

Well, don’t be fooled, this still reads like a na story, and truly it should have been one, because the characters do not read like adults, but rather they should have been written as early twenty somethings.

Things I didn’t like about this book:

1- Lottie. She’s a horrible person in the beginning of this book (see reason #2). She selfish, hostile, immature (she should be 23, not 28): and is a toxic individual. I avoid people like her irl, and I most certainly don’t want to read about someone like her as a fmc.

2- this story is way too choppy. It reads as if Quinn just threw in pre-written snippets throughout, but didn’t take the time to fully finesse them. Many of these snippet scenes read as if they came from the author’s scene pile, but she forgot to go back and apply the character arcs. (Yes, I know many people do this - and I’m not knocking the writing technique - just go back and make sure the scene gels with the arc.)

3- MQ should stick with NA. I didn’t buy that the mc’s were 35 and 28. There is no way a 35 yo billionaire would be acting like he does. The suspension of belief required here was just too much. These two are so immature, it’s painful.

4- way, way too many eff bombs. Like really - an unnecessary, distracting amount. Just because the characters are adults doesn’t mean they need to be written so narrowly. Who talks like this in real life? No one I know.

5- way, way too many oral sexy times. Really, I just wanted them to do the deed already. Scene after scene of oral sex got super annoying - all I could think was: you’re grown adults, you want each other, just get it on already - geez. And what 35 yo man is down for some dry humping? Is she serious with this? Are these mc’s supposed to be 16?

So there you have it. I haven’t written this much in a review in a while lol, but I really was disappointed - and mostly annoyed, but I did finish this hot mess.

Save your time and money and skip this one, and pick up a Quinn na romance instead - if you like that genre. She’s much better at those, truly. For myself, I think I’m done with trying a MQ adult genre, still too immature for this romance reader.

One disappointed star.

This was a really enjoyable and fun book to read on a lazy Sunday and I was especially happy to find it on Kindle Unlimited 😊

✅ I LIKED HUXLEY'S inner thoughts at the beginning of the book - his POV was definitely my favorite and I just liked how he approached his business deals with such a logical but cut throat mentality. I found his voice more humorous than the typical "alpha businessman" love interests you read about

🆗 LOTTIE WAS ENTERTAINING but her characterization was a bit confusing. She was a self-characterized "doormat", but I actually found her to be incredibly confrontational, especially when it came to Huxley. So it was harder to understand her.

✅ I WAS WORRIED this was going to be wayyy too cliche but it surprised me with some of the unique situations this couple was put into 😂 Ovearll, while there were some cliche parts, I thought the romance still stood out from other fake-dating books I've read

✅ I REALLY LIKED THE ROMANCE and will definitely be picking up more of Meghan Quinn's books in the future 💕 There was a decent amount of tension building up to them being together, some really heartwarming scenes, but then also a lot of steam too!

🆗 THE ENDING was just okay... at first, I thought there was going to be minimal drama with how things were going, but then that didn't end up being the case 😣 It all came together eventually, but it's just hard to find a romcom where I don't find the drama that causes the inevitable fallout too over to the top and obnoxious

Overall, I read this book in one sitting today so obviously I really liked it even though it wasn't perfect. I think it could have been a little bit shorter but I would definitely recommend it if you're looking for a fake-dating romcom with lots of banter, lots of tension and steamy scenes, an alpha-hole businessman love interest, and a cute ending!
